title: Community-Acquired Pneumonia
scenario: A 72-year-old male presents to the emergency department with a 4-day history of productive cough, fever, and increasing shortness of breath. He reports rust-colored sputum and pain in the right side of his chest that worsens with deep breathing.

lines: 72-year-old male brought in by wife for 4 days of productive cough with rust-colored sputum, fever, chills, and worsening dyspnea. Reports pleuritic right-sided chest pain. Coarse crackles and diminished breath sounds auscultated over the right lower lobe. Skin warm and flushed. Alert but appears fatigued and mildly confused per wife, who states this is new.
IV access obtained. Blood cultures x2, sputum culture, CBC, and chest x-ray ordered. O2 started at 3L per nasal cannula. Cardiac monitor and continuous pulse oximetry applied.
IV ceftriaxone and oral azithromycin administered per order after cultures drawn. Acetaminophen given for fever. 500 mL normal saline bolus infusing.
Client reports breathing is easier and chest pain reduced. Coughing up moderate sputum effectively. Oriented to person, place, and time. Breath sounds improving over right base.
Normal saline 500 mL IV bolus, then 100 mL/hr
Acetaminophen 650 mg PO every 6 hours PRN fever
Titrate oxygen to keep SpO2 at or above 92%
Blood cultures x2 before first antibiotic dose
Incentive spirometry every 1 hour while awake

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.rationale: Hypoxia, tachypnea, high fever, and new confusion signal severe pneumonia and possible sepsis requiring immediate intervention. Rust-colored sputum and a mildly low blood pressure are expected findings that warrant monitoring but are less urgent.

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: For each finding, click to specify whether it supports a diagnosis of pneumonia, systemic infection/sepsis, or both. Each finding may support more than one.

rows.text: Diminished breath sounds over the right lower lobe

children.rationale: Focal diminished breath sounds are a localized lung finding of pneumonia; elevated lactate and new confusion reflect systemic hypoperfusion and organ dysfunction of sepsis. Leukocytosis with neutrophilia supports both the pulmonary infection and the systemic inflammatory response.

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: Complete the sentence. The nurse determines that the priority problem is {1}, and the first action is to {2}.
children.rationale: The most immediate threat is impaired gas exchange, shown by an SpO2 of 86% and a respiratory rate of 30, so applying oxygen takes priority over pain relief, fever control, or diagnostics.

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: For each intervention, click to specify whether it is indicated or contraindicated for this client.

rows.text: Draw blood cultures before starting antibiotics
Position the client in high Fowler's
Withhold antibiotics until sputum culture results return
Restrict oral fluids to reduce secretions

children.rationale: Cultures before antibiotics, upright positioning, and incentive spirometry all support oxygenation and targeted treatment. Delaying antibiotics in suspected sepsis and restricting fluids that help mobilize secretions are contraindicated.

children.subject: Pharmacology
children.stem: After initiating the ordered treatment, which actions should the nurse take? Select all that apply.

options.text: Ensure blood cultures were obtained before the first antibiotic dose
Titrate oxygen to maintain SpO2 at or above 92%
Monitor for signs of an allergic reaction to the antibiotic
Reassess vital signs and lactate for response to the fluid bolus
Hold the fluid bolus until the fever resolves
Place the client on strict bed rest with no repositioning

children.rationale: The nurse confirms cultures preceded antibiotics, titrates oxygen, watches for drug reactions, and evaluates the response to fluid resuscitation. Holding fluids in a hypotensive, high-lactate client and forbidding repositioning would worsen perfusion and oxygenation.

children.subject: Medical-Surgical
children.stem: Which findings indicate the treatment has been effective? Select all that apply.

options.text: Client is oriented to person, place, and time

children.rationale: Improved oxygenation, respiratory rate, fever, and resolution of confusion all show the infection and hypoxia are responding to treatment. A rising heart rate would suggest worsening sepsis, not improvement.
